listing.name: GitHub
listing.description:
The GitHub Power-Up for Trello let’s teams track everything that’s going on in GitHub directly from their Trello boards.  Bring perspective to your codebase by attaching pull requests, issues, branches, and more directly to their respective cards.  In a glance, see whether a PR has been merged, the status of checks, who’s assigned to a PR, and more. Checks will also display as visual badges on the front of cards color coded to their status.

- Attach branches, commits, issues and pull requests directly to cards.
- See the status of pull requests on the front of cards.
- Identify cards that have not passed their checks with color coded badges that display on the front of cards.
- Developers and managers can easily jump into GitHub to work on assigned tasks in a single click.
- Associate one or more GitHub repositories with a board.
- The GitHub Power-Up supports both GitHub and GitHub Enterprise instances.

![screenshot](https://github.trello.services/images/screenshots/GitHub_1.jpg)

![screenshot](https://github.trello.services/images/screenshots/GitHub_2.jpg)

![screenshot](https://github.trello.services/images/screenshots/GitHub_3.jpg)
listing.overview: Attach branches, commits, issues, & pull requests to cards, and see the status of pull requests on your boards.

# Summary:

TEEP 2025 topics advance O-RAN automation and intelligence by enhancing rApp orchestration, WiFi and digital twin integration, dynamic network deployment, and AI-driven configuration debugging. Aqshal, Nadya, and Rossi worked on rApp deployment and validation within the SMO framework, improving orchestration, troubleshooting, and reliability. Edgrant and Justin developed O-RAN–compliant WiFi adapters and digital twin simulators for realistic RF modeling and indoor localization. Fata and Daffa improved Large Language Models (LLMs) for automated 5G configuration debugging using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Agni enhanced Network Functions Orchestration (NFO) with an Auto Homing mechanism that enables dynamic cluster selection for flexible, efficient deployment. Together, these works advance automation, integration, and AI-driven intelligence in O-RAN networks.

- *Topic*: Project Management and Documentation Guidelines for Thesis/Paper Submissions
- *Summary*: The meeting introduced guidelines and templates for repository structure, project documentation, and citation management, with an emphasis on separating documentation components and ensuring all work is aligned for thesis and conference paper submissions. Key discussion points included making the repository private, using the labs account, decoupling installation guides, and utilizing AI to draft initial documentation sections. The weekly Wednesday meeting with the Professor was established as the progress checking and review point.

---

### Project Documentation Guidelines (Thesis/Paper Submissions)

- Discussion Points
  - The project documentation and study notes will be used for thesis writing and conference paper submissions.
  - The project documentation acts as an **umbrella** document, covering the project's background knowledge and the larger study.
  - The documentation should be structured to include:
    - The **background problem** and its importance for the scenario.
    - The **contributions** made to solve the problem (what was built).
    - The **challenges** faced in building the contribution (reasons why it's hard).
  - The information needs to be **decoupled**; installation guides for specific components (e.g., Near RT-RIC, SMO, NS3) must be documented separately as Component A, B, C, etc.
  - The main project documentation will link to the combination of these separate component guides via **hyperlink** attachment.
  - The **NSTC project proposal** can be used as a starting point to extract the background, importance, and contributions sections.
  - Attendees are encouraged to use **AI (like ChatGPT)** to draft and highlight the initial points for the four sections (background, importance, contributions, challenges) and then discuss and enhance them.
  - All code submissions must eventually have an associated **class diagram** for the Professor's review.
  - For citation management, a **.bib file** must be used for all references to ensure compatibility with LaTeX for thesis and paper writing.

---

### Repository Structure and Management

- Discussion Points
  - The repository for the project must always be set as **private** on GitHub. Do not make it public.
  - All work must be conducted using the **labs account**, not personal accounts.
  - Each individual attendee is expected to use their own **branch** for work and daily plan logs.
  - Meeting minutes should be kept separate from Trello/comment sections to avoid making the logs too long. They should be placed in a dedicated folder or file, such as meeting_minutes or `milestones.md`.
  - The daily logs and milestone files are based on the same template used in Trello and will be synced with Trello in the future.
  - When referencing commits, always use the **full commit hash** or the **first 7-digit commit hash (BLOB)** to track progress and prevent loss of work if file names are modified on the master branch.
  - Before creating a new repository for a project, check if a repository already exists; the preferred action is to create a new **branch** in the existing repo.

- Progress Report
- I have learned the overview of the O1 Interface based on the _O-RAN Work Group 10 (OAM for O-RAN) - O-RAN O1 Interface Specification_ document [1]
- I've created my study notes summarizing the key points of the O1 Interface \_https://github.com/bmw-ece-ntust/internship/blob/2025-TEEP-2-Edgrant/docs/StudyNotes/09_O1-Interface.md
- Discussion Points
- The wifi adapter has 3 phases:
- **Phase 1:** The target is to be able to send Performance Management (PM) data (RSSI, Client Count, etc.) to the SMO formatted according to the specification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- The data will be sent as a file-based report, which is a JSON file containing the crawled data.
- The SMO will process this data and store it in InfluxDB.
- The data will be sent using VES (VNF Event Stream) format.
- It will use the SFTP to send data to the SMO.
- **Phase 2:** The target is to be able to edit the wifi adapter configuration using Netconf, according to the spesification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- **Phase 3:** The target is to be able to use the SMO to control the wifi adapter as a MNS producer, allowing the SMO to manage the wifi adapter's configuration and performance using the O1 interface.
- Action Items
- Learn more details about Performance Management (PM)
- Learn more about how to implement VES format for the JSON file to be sent to the SMO.

- Discussion Points
- The wifi adapter has 3 phases:
- **Phase 1:** The target is to be able to send Performance Management (PM) data (RSSI, Client Count, etc.) to the SMO formatted according to the specification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- The data will be sent as a file-based report, which is a JSON file containing the crawled data.
- The SMO will process this data and store it in InfluxDB.
- The data will be sent using VES (VNF Event Stream) format.
- It will use the SFTP to send data to the SMO.
- **Phase 2:** The target is to be able to edit the wifi adapter configuration using Netconf, according to the spesification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- **Phase 3:** The target is to be able to use the SMO to control the wifi adapter as a MNS producer, allowing the SMO to manage the wifi adapter's configuration and performance using the O1 interface.
- Action Items
- Learn more details about Performance Management (PM)
- Learn more about how to implement VES format for the JSON file to be sent to the SMO.

- I have learned the overview of the O1 Interface based on the _O-RAN Work Group 10 (OAM for O-RAN) - O-RAN O1 Interface Specification_ document [1]
- I've created my study notes summarizing the key points of the O1 Interface \_https://github.com/bmw-ece-ntust/internship/blob/2025-TEEP-2-Edgrant/docs/StudyNotes/09_O1-Interface.md
- Discussion Points
- The wifi adapter has 3 phases:
- **Phase 1:** The target is to be able to send Performance Management (PM) data (RSSI, Client Count, etc.) to the SMO formatted according to the specification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- The data will be sent as a file-based report, which is a JSON file containing the crawled data.
- The SMO will process this data and store it in InfluxDB.
- The data will be sent using VES (VNF Event Stream) format.
- It will use the SFTP to send data to the SMO.
- **Phase 2:** The target is to be able to edit the wifi adapter configuration using Netconf, according to the spesification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- **Phase 3:** The target is to be able to use the SMO to control the wifi adapter as a MNS producer, allowing the SMO to manage the wifi adapter's configuration and performance using the O1 interface.
- Action Items
- Learn more details about Performance Management (PM)
- Learn more about how to implement VES format for the JSON file to be sent to the SMO.

- Progress Report
- I have learned the overview of the O1 Interface based on the _O-RAN Work Group 10 (OAM for O-RAN) - O-RAN O1 Interface Specification_ document [1]
- I've created my study notes summarizing the key points of the O1 Interface \_https://github.com/bmw-ece-ntust/internship/blob/2025-TEEP-2-Edgrant/docs/StudyNotes/09_O1-Interface.md
- Discussion Points
- The wifi adapter has 3 phases:
- **Phase 1:** The target is to be able to send Performance Management (PM) data (RSSI, Client Count, etc.) to the SMO formatted according to the specification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- The data will be sent as a file-based report, which is a JSON file containing the crawled data.
- The SMO will process this data and store it in InfluxDB.
- The data will be sent using VES (VNF Event Stream) format.
- It will use the SFTP to send data to the SMO.
- **Phase 2:** The target is to be able to edit the wifi adapter configuration using Netconf, according to the spesification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- **Phase 3:** The target is to be able to use the SMO to control the wifi adapter as a MNS producer, allowing the SMO to manage the wifi adapter's configuration and performance using the O1 interface.
- Action Items
- Learn more details about Performance Management (PM)
- Learn more about how to implement VES format for the JSON file to be sent to the SMO.

- O-RAN software community as a way to reduce operator dependence on vendors, increase cost-effectiveness, and expedite research.

# Probation:

The probation duration is started `the moment you're accepted` for this internship program until 3-4 months (can be negotiated). Your performance during the probation will **determine whether you’re accepted/rejected for the onsite internship** in our lab.

Please pay attention with the following steps:

1. Create your personal Trello card - [template](https://trello.com/c/u9sGqbL3 "‌").
2. Finish the 1st Checklist within 1 weeks*.
3. **Find a mentor** to discuss about your milestone and topic.
4. Write your Milestones (monthly target) on the checklist section following the template below.
5. Write your daily for intern project & class course on the activity section following the [template](https://trello.com/c/u9sGqbL3#comment-659d890649307cc45b86ce29 "‌").
6. Input your work in Trello using Hyperlink : [https://drive.google.com/file/d/1OaBAXgMUCvCUQz4GsodeCcIdW4o-_wWb/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1OaBAXgMUCvCUQz4GsodeCcIdW4o-_wWb/view?usp=sharing "smartCard-inline")
7. Contact [Ian Joseph Chandra](mailto:d11202805@gapps.ntust.edu.tw "‌") as soon as you have any questions.

**Note**:

\* The deadline can be negotiate if you’re in exam week (discuss it with your mentors)

# Internship:

It applies on `remote probation`, `remote internship`, & `onsite internship`. Any violation will causes **immediate disqualification**.

1. **DO NOT** take any other internship `from probation - end of internship` duration.
2. You will work from **Monday - Friday from 09.00 - 17.00**.
3. **Check-in** at _your Trello card Activity_ **before 9:00**, and write down your `daily plan` or `Backlog`.
4. **Push** all of your works to _your Github Branch,_ including the daily logs (you can copy it from the trello)
5. **Check-out** at _your Trello card Activity_ **after 17:00** by attaching the `hyperlink result` (as evidence of your work).
6. Write any documentation of your project on the [BMW Internship Github](https://github.com/bmw-ece-ntust/internship "‌") - [Instruction](https://github.com/bmw-ece-ntust/internship?tab=readme-ov-file#1-introduction "‌").
7. **Have a weekly meeting** with your mentor & write the meeting minutes (complete with your **action items** for the next week) on your Trello card activity.
   **Note**: You can have **daily stand-ups** if you and your mentor want, but weekly meetings are highly recommended. Check with your mentor for the schedule. You can also create a new card to keep track of your weekly meetings.

# **Internship Outcome**:

1. IEEE conference paper report, detailing the research and development carried out during the internship.
2. Complete source code of the project was uploaded to GitHub with proper documentation.
3. System architecture diagram to represent the overall design and component interaction.
4. Message sequence chart to illustrate the flow of communication between system modules.
5. Installation guide to assist users in setting up and running the project.
6. Demo video to showcase the project’s features and functionality.
7. Testimonial video,
8. Summary in Google Docs for government report.

# End of Intern

1. Verify the **deliverables** in your card with the mentor;
2. Finish all tasks on your Trello card checklists;
3. Create **internship experience sharing** in two formats:
   1. Text in Google Docs link & your card section activity;
   2. Video testimony on [Youtube](http://youtube.com "‌").
4. Complete the [TEEP survey form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSdWLiwlq39icJ-ulSeVIIHkzcu01MwK-xSO_9tMzItofZt0hQ/viewform "‌");
5. Complete the [mentors assessment form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeJ5ZNKkrz27HFsO2ZFiU-mB2DwD8yFyf45zqdxJqjnnyWVLA/viewform "‌");
6. Get the certificate for your internship (you can provide the template if needed).

# Final Presentation

# 2. Arrival Guide

When you arrived in Taiwan, please follow these steps as part of the administration procedure. Things to bring and buy can be seen through  [arrival guide at Github ](https://github.com/bmw-ece-ntust/internship/blob/master/arrival-guide.md "‌")

## Taiwan Sim Card:

1. SimCard is needed for you to make a bank account so as you arrive at the airport go choose a simcard booth. **PRO TIP!** : Just buy the 3 or 5 days simcard because Taiwan number is just needed to make the postbank.
2. Purchase `IF Card` from the mentor's mutual connections (Currently: [Ivan Tantio](http://wa.me/886908489336 "‌")).
3. Purchase roaming E-Sim from your original country.

## Transportation Card:

EZCard is a e-money card that is very versatile, it can help you save time in EZCard-enabled stores (like FamilyMart,etc). EZCard can be bought on local stores, with a price, and also can be topped-up on the same stores. One of the most important use of EZCard is to rent a bike at **YouBike**

1. Download YouBike App on [Play Store](https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&source=web&rct=j&opi=89978449&url=https://play.google.com/store/apps/details%3Fid%3Dtw.com.youbike.plus%26hl%3Den&ved=2ahUKEwiMyZ2O86-HAxXRc_UHHTZNBzgQFnoECBkQAQ&usg=AOvVaw16DZW_Y0spFtdONtmLJwPU "‌") or [App Store](https://www.google.com/url?sa=t&source=web&rct=j&opi=89978449&url=https://apps.apple.com/tw/app/youbike%25E5%25BE%25AE%25E7%25AC%2591%25E5%2596%25AE%25E8%25BB%258A-%25E5%25AE%2598%25E6%2596%25B9%25E7%2589%2588/id1483423095&ved=2ahUKEwiMyZ2O86-HAxXRc_UHHTZNBzgQFnoECCkQAQ&usg=AOvVaw2GXG7otb833bUmTBPC2jZO "‌").
2. Register yourself using your UI Number as the identification number.
3. Register your EZCard number to the YouBike App to enable it.

‌

## Accommodation\*\*:\*\*

1. Dormitory facilities are not available this year. Interns must arrange their own accommodation through platforms such as [591.com.tw](http://591.com.tw/ "‌"), Facebook Marketplace, etc.

Recommendation Purchase place:

1. Dorm-3 [Stationery Store](https://maps.app.goo.gl/WkQnDenJ2wB1Udrg6 "‌") at Basement;
2. [Green Store](https://maps.app.goo.gl/UdwgDXAre8YemjYL8 "‌")
3. [Carrefour at Qizhang](https://maps.app.goo.gl/Rh9b58MUcTMrBvC3A "‌")

## UI Number

1. Go to [National Immigration Agency](https://maps.app.goo.gl/UjSH7WFFF382XmKi9 "‌") and create your UI Number.
   1. You will need to take queue number first, prepare:
      1. **Passport**;
      2. **Copy of your passport** (available photocopy machine on the spot).
      3. **UI Number Request form**, you can get this form the Agency or the NTUST’s OIA Office (we attached a map below).
   2. UI Number is **your own personal identification number**, please keep the certificate as your identification card back in your country.

**Note**: `Come in the morning`, otherwise you will wait a long time or even not get a queue number.

## Bank Account:

- *Summary*: The meeting introduced guidelines and templates for repository structure, project documentation, and citation management, with an emphasis on separating documentation components and ensuring all work is aligned for thesis and conference paper submissions. The weekly Wednesday meeting with the Professor was established as the progress checking and review point.

---

### Project Documentation Guidelines (Thesis/Paper Submissions)

- Discussion Points
  - The project documentation and study notes will be used for thesis writing and conference paper submissions.
  - The project documentation acts as an **umbrella** document, covering the project's background knowledge and the larger study.
  - The documentation should be structured to include:
    - The **background problem** and its importance for the scenario.
    - The **contributions** made to solve the problem (what was built).
    - The **challenges** faced in building the contribution (reasons why it's hard).
  - The information needs to be **decoupled**; installation guides for specific components (e.g., Near RT-RIC, SMO, NS3) must be documented separately as Component A, B, C, etc.
  - The main project documentation will link to the combination of these separate component guides via **hyperlink** attachment.
  - The **NSTC project proposal** can be used as a starting point to extract the background, importance, and contributions sections.
  - Attendees are encouraged to use **AI (like ChatGPT)** to draft and highlight the initial points for the four sections (background, importance, contributions, challenges) and then discuss and enhance them.
  - All code submissions must eventually have an associated **class diagram** for the Professor's review.
  - For citation management, a **.bib file** must be used for all references to ensure compatibility with LaTeX for thesis and paper writing.

---

### Repository Structure and Management

- Discussion Points
  - The repository for the project must always be set as **private** on GitHub. Do not make it public.
  - All work must be conducted using the **labs account**, not personal accounts.
  - Each individual attendee is expected to use their own **branch** for work and daily plan logs.
  - Meeting minutes should be kept separate from Trello/comment sections to avoid making the logs too long. They should be placed in a dedicated folder or file, such as meeting_minutes or `milestones.md`.
  - The daily logs and milestone files are based on the same template used in Trello and will be synced with Trello in the future.
  - When referencing commits, always use the **full commit hash** or the **first 7-digit commit hash (BLOB)** to track progress and prevent loss of work if file names are modified on the master branch.
  - Before creating a new repository for a project, check if a repository already exists; the preferred action is to create a new **branch** in the existing repo.

## 2025/10/27-00.00

- _Recording_: N/A
- _Attendees_: Maria Amparo Canaveras Galdon, Johnson, Evan (M11402811)
- _Topic_: Data Processing, System Model Architecture, and Integration with SMO (O-RAN)
- _Summary_:
  The meeting focused on three primary areas: progress on data preparation and JSON formatting for inconsistencies, the design and refinement of the system model architecture integrating SMO and expert systems, and the discussion on interface standards (O1, A1) and automation requirements. Each participant outlined updates and challenges, while action items were set for the next meeting on Wednesday.

---

### **Discussion Points**

#### **1. Data Preparation and JSON Structure**

- Evan reported progress on generating inconsistent cases between CU and DU modules, totaling approximately 300 valid instances, with 147 identified errors.
- Maria emphasized ensuring uniform JSON formatting for logs and configurations, recommending that multiple parameters be stored as arrays or JSON lists.
- Evan confirmed plans to generate more error cases within the week and will maintain consistency in the data structure.
- Maria suggested documenting JSON paths for parameters to facilitate clarity in the pipeline and future discussions.

#### **2. System Model and Workflow**

- Johnson shared progress on the overall system model integrating CU, DU, and RU components under the NG-RAN framework.
- The system aims to automate configuration correction and log generation via an expert system that may include LLM-based reasoning modules.
- The professor recommended integrating a standardized interface (O1) to enhance automation and reduce manual intervention.
- Maria advised reorganizing the diagram for clarity—ensuring logical left-to-right, top-to-bottom flow—and incorporating meaningful icons (e.g., logs, reasoning traces).
- She requested the [http://Draw.io](http://Draw.io "smartCard-inline")  source file from Johnson to refine the visual representation and improve interpretability.
- Johnson noted that professor feedback emphasized automation through standard interfaces and incorporating topology and inventory modules (TIV) for configuration storage.
- The logs will be transmitted through the ORVIS collector, and Johnson is considering API-based communication for integration with the training pipeline.

#### **3. Training Pipeline and Expert System Integration**

- Maria highlighted the distinction between the **training phase** (offline supervised fine-tuning using historical logs and configurations) and the **inference phase** (real-time LLM serving as part of the expert system).
- The LLM will replace one of the expert system modules, serving to automate reasoning and configuration decisions based on received data.
- The professor recommended including both training and inference components in the same system diagram for clarity.
- Maria explained that the LLM agent within the expert system will communicate with SMO using defined O-RAN interfaces (A1 for policy guidance, O1 for configuration and fault management).
- The conversation detailed the need to explore how SMO exchanges data with external ML systems through APIs or RESTful interfaces.
- Johnson confirmed that part of the training configuration will be modularized, possibly implemented via an R-app, and the supervised fine-tuned model will issue new configurations through O1Netconf.
- Maria reiterated that while the lab focuses on synthetic data for now, the real system will rely on historical logs for reasoning trace generation and model fine-tuning.

#### **4. Writing Progress and Documentation**

- Johnson updated on thesis progress, noting completion of architecture, reasoning trace, and error log generation sections.
- References are still missing and will be added per professor’s feedback.
- Maria plans to contribute references and assist in refining sections related to reasoning and result interpretation.
- The team aims to document how the data and pipeline outputs can be shared or exposed for research collaboration.

---

### **Action Items**

- **Evan (M11402811):**
  - [ ] Generate additional CU/DU inconsistency cases for testing.
  - [ ] Ensure logs and misconfigured parameters follow the unified JSON structure.
  - [ ] Email Maria the link to the GitHub repository with the JSONL format.
- **Johnson:**
  - [ ] Send the [http://Draw.io](http://Draw.io "smartCard-inline")  file of the system model to Maria for refinement.

- Discussion Points
- The wifi adapter has 3 phases:
- **Phase 1:** The target is to be able to send Performance Management (PM) data (RSSI, Client Count, etc.) to the SMO formatted according to the specification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- The data will be sent as a file-based report, which is a JSON file containing the crawled data.
- The SMO will process this data and store it in InfluxDB.
- The data will be sent using VES (VNF Event Stream) format.
- It will use the SFTP to send data to the SMO.
- **Phase 2:** The target is to be able to edit the wifi adapter configuration using Netconf, according to the spesification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- **Phase 3:** The target is to be able to use the SMO to control the wifi adapter as a MNS producer, allowing the SMO to manage the wifi adapter's configuration and performance using the O1 interface.

- Discussion Points
- In the Aruba Crawler, the shell file loops calling the Python script,
- This is not ideal for the Unifi Crawler because the Unifi Crawler need to log in which will take approximately 1 minute before it can scrape the data
- The Unifi Crawler could be implemented by looping calling the Python script in the shell file if the crawling period is longer than 1 minute.
- Action Items
- Install InfluxDB in a server
- Add the data to the InfluxDB after scraping
- Try to run the script for 24 hours

- Discussion Points
- The wifi adapter has 3 phases:
- **Phase 1:** The target is to be able to send Performance Management (PM) data (RSSI, Client Count, etc.) to the SMO formatted according to the specification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- The data will be sent as a file-based report, which is a JSON file containing the crawled data.
- The SMO will process this data and store it in InfluxDB.
- The data will be sent using VES (VNF Event Stream) format.
- It will use the SFTP to send data to the SMO.
- **Phase 2:** The target is to be able to edit the wifi adapter configuration using Netconf, according to the spesification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- **Phase 3:** The target is to be able to use the SMO to control the wifi adapter as a MNS producer, allowing the SMO to manage the wifi adapter's configuration and performance using the O1 interface.

- Discussion Points
- The wifi adapter has 3 phases:
- **Phase 1:** The target is to be able to send Performance Management (PM) data (RSSI, Client Count, etc.) to the SMO formatted according to the specification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- The data will be sent as a file-based report, which is a JSON file containing the crawled data.
- The SMO will process this data and store it in InfluxDB.
- The data will be sent using VES (VNF Event Stream) format.
- It will use the SFTP to send data to the SMO.
- **Phase 2:** The target is to be able to edit the wifi adapter configuration using Netconf, according to the spesification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- **Phase 3:** The target is to be able to use the SMO to control the wifi adapter as a MNS producer, allowing the SMO to manage the wifi adapter's configuration and performance using the O1 interface.
- Action Items
- Learn more details about Performance Management (PM)
- Learn more about how to implement VES format for the JSON file to be sent to the SMO.

# Probation:

1. Register a [HackMD](https://hackmd.io/ "‌") account & setup a nickname.
2. Create your personal Trello card based on the [template](https://trello.com/c/u9sGqbL3 "‌").
3. Setup your 4 weeks probation topic with your mentor*.
4. Report your status with mentor every week.
5. Contact Prof. Ray as soon as you have any questions.

**Notes**:
\* it’s better you design your topic align with your Bachelor Thesis (if any).

# Internship:

1. You will work from Monday - Friday from 09.00 - 17.00
2. Check-in at _your Trello card_ **before 9:00**, and write down your daily plan.
3. Check-out at _your Trello card_ **after 17:00**, and summarize the works that have been done.
4. Push your update on [BMW HackMD book](https://hackmd.io/@ianjoseph/bmw-book "‌") to [BMW Lab Github](https://github.com/NTUST-BMW-Lab "‌") & **copy the commit hyperlink** to your Trello.
5. Upload any code modification to [BMW Lab Github](https://github.com/NTUST-BMW-Lab "‌").
6. Report your status online using WebEx during the weekly meeting. Summarize the action items in their Meeting of Minutes.

# End of Intern

1. Verify the study note on [BMW HackMD book](https://hackmd.io/@ianjoseph/bmw-book "‌") with your mentor.
2. Finish all tasks on your Trello card checklists.
3. Create **internship experience sharing** in two formats:
   1. Text in HackMD
   2. Video testimonial on [Youtube](http://youtube.com "‌")
4. Complete the [TEEP survey form](https://forms.gle/VyvNpgahqahNeNr96 "‌").
5. Get the certificate for your internship (you can provide me with the template if needed).

# Summary:

TEEP 2025 topics advance O-RAN automation and intelligence by enhancing rApp orchestration, WiFi and digital twin integration, dynamic network deployment, and AI-driven configuration debugging. Aqshal, Nadya, and Rossi worked on rApp deployment and validation within the SMO framework, improving orchestration, troubleshooting, and reliability. Edgrant and Justin developed O-RAN–compliant WiFi adapters and digital twin simulators for realistic RF modeling and indoor localization. Fata and Daffa improved Large Language Models (LLMs) for automated 5G configuration debugging using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Agni enhanced Network Functions Orchestration (NFO) with an Auto Homing mechanism that enables dynamic cluster selection for flexible, efficient deployment. Together, these works advance automation, integration, and AI-driven intelligence in O-RAN networks.

- Progress Report
- I have learned the overview of the O1 Interface based on the _O-RAN Work Group 10 (OAM for O-RAN) - O-RAN O1 Interface Specification_ document [1]
- I've created my study notes summarizing the key points of the O1 Interface \_https://github.com/bmw-ece-ntust/internship/blob/2025-TEEP-2-Edgrant/docs/StudyNotes/09_O1-Interface.md
- Discussion Points
- The wifi adapter has 3 phases:
- **Phase 1:** The target is to be able to send Performance Management (PM) data (RSSI, Client Count, etc.) to the SMO formatted according to the specification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- The data will be sent as a file-based report, which is a JSON file containing the crawled data.
- The SMO will process this data and store it in InfluxDB.
- The data will be sent using VES (VNF Event Stream) format.
- It will use the SFTP to send data to the SMO.
- **Phase 2:** The target is to be able to edit the wifi adapter configuration using Netconf, according to the spesification in the WG10 O1 interface document.
- **Phase 3:** The target is to be able to use the SMO to control the wifi adapter as a MNS producer, allowing the SMO to manage the wifi adapter's configuration and performance using the O1 interface.
- Action Items
- Learn more details about Performance Management (PM)
- Learn more about how to implement VES format for the JSON file to be sent to the SMO.

Title: **AI-Driven Evolution of Mobile Networks: Trends, Toolkits, and Deployment Frameworks.**

This study focuses on the following key topics:

- **Analysis of AI Technology Development Trends in Mobile Networks:** This involves analyzing the development trends and global research directions of AI technologies in mobile networks, consolidating application patterns and development trajectories of AI in mobile network scenarios, and exploring the technological evolution priorities of relevant standardization bodies (such as 3GPP, O-RAN, and AI-RAN) to establish a solid research foundation.
- **Evaluation of AI Toolkits and Application Potential for Mobile Networks:** This includes a functional analysis and potential assessment of AI development toolkits relevant to mobile networks (e.g., NVIDIA Aerial SDK), examining their technical feasibility, supported task domains, and deployment limitations within mobile network applications, and proposing appropriate application scenarios and integration strategies.
- **Modeling of AI Deployment and Computational Requirements Across Mobile Network Nodes:** This part models and evaluates the deployment requirements and computational resource needs of AI models across various mobile network nodes, including aspects such as latency tolerance, bandwidth limitations, data collection types, and inference cycles, aiming to establish deployment conditions and resource allocation recommendations to strengthen feasibility analysis.
- **System Integration Recommendations and Future Development Directions:** This section provides holistic system integration suggestions and outlines future development directions, including integration solutions of AI technologies within mobile networks, demonstrative architecture proposals, potential implementation challenges, and corresponding strategies, serving as a critical reference for intelligent network technology planning and policy promotion.

# Bachelor Thesis

## TITLE:

UE Indoor Positioning using WiFi + BLE for MIMO Energy Saving

## PURPOSE:

Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) AP or BTS has several antennas that shoot the beam (called beam forming) of the signal into specific angle and direction.

Enhancing the accuracy of beam forming by detecting the position of the User Equipment (UE).

Reducing the power consumption by only activating the antenna that directing to the UE during the data transmission.

## MILESTONES

1. General UE positioning --> Prof. Leu's Ph.D. (Mr. Muiz) is working for this one
2. Position-based Antenna Configuration for Energy Saving
3. Angle utilization for Position detection + Beam Accuracy enhancement.

## CURRENT PROGRESS

1. WiFi + BLE RSSI crawler using Android:
   [GitHub - bmw-ece-ntust/ips-android-crawler](https://github.com/bmw-ece-ntust/ips-android-crawler "‌")

### Journal

- [Link to TUD overleaf](https://tex.zih.tu-dresden.de/project/63da36fd10abaf00a05107eb "‌") - Prof Ray can access

### Testimony:

My internship at NTUST through the NTSCs International Internship Pilot Program has been transformative, encapsulating significant achievements in a condensed timeframe.

The integration of LiteOn 7.2 with OpenAirInterface was a key technical focus. Collaborating closely with Summer, successful debugging sessions at the LiteOn Lab and subsequent E2E traffic transmission highlighted the program's commitment to practical learning.

Academic contributions were notable, especially the transition of a joint paper into a journal publication. Enhancing plot quality and clarity was a collaborative effort, enriched by discussions with Prof. Ray and fellow students.

Industry engagements, particularly the 5G ACIA Taipei Event 2023, provided insights into local and global landscapes. Collaborations with local companies and networking with industry leaders like Nokia broadened my understanding.

Mentorship and collaboration with local students, including supporting Akmal's master's defense and discussing his future prospects, offered valuable insights. Connecting with peers facilitated a rich cultural exchange, contributing to a holistic understanding of Taiwan.

The deployment of GeniusCore, lab relocation, and participation in IEEE CCNC showcased the program's commitment to beyond 5G technologies and global perspectives.

In conclusion, the NTSCs International Internship Pilot Program at NTUST has been an enriching journey. The program's commitment to practical learning, academic excellence, industry engagement, and cultural exchange has significantly contributed to building, strengthening international academical connections as well as my personal growth as a researcher.

### Part 1 (Study the official version ns3) (1/26~1/30 (3day))

### Part 2 ( WiFi experiment )

### 0. background survey:

- 802.11e

### 1. Prepare Configuration File

The configuration file should include the coordinates topology information of the WiFi nodes, 802.11e configuration parameters, and any other necessary network configuration information such as channel selection, transmission rate, etc.

### 2. Configure NS-3 Network

Based on the configuration file, you need to use NS-3's API to configure the network. Here is a basic process:

- **Create Nodes and WiFi Devices:** Use `NodeContainer` to create APs and STAs.
- **Configure WiFi Model:** Choose 802.11e and configure relevant parameters, including CW\_min and CW\_max.
- **Set Position Information:** Use `MobilityHelper` to set the positions of the nodes.
- **Establish Application Layer Protocol:** Configure the data transmission model as needed, such as UDP or TCP connections.

### 3. Run Simulation and Collect Data

- **Start Simulation:** Use `Simulator::Run()` to start the simulation.
- **Data Collection:** Use `FlowMonitor` to collect metrics such as throughput, delay, and packet loss rate for each STA.

### 4. External Algorithm to Dynamically Adjust CW Values

- **External Algorithm Interface:** You need to define an interface that allows the external algorithm to dynamically adjust CW\_min and CW\_max values during the simulation. This may involve implementing a custom module inside NS-3 or using existing APIs for adjustments.
- **Real-time Data Feedback:** Ensure the algorithm can adjust parameters based on real-time collected data.
